Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 53, "heading": "CHAPTER 51. THE BEGINNING OF A LONGER JOURNEY", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u053-b0057", "target": "— И вы хотите, чтобы я поехал с вами? — спросил я, видя, что он что-то недосказал.", "source_sha256": "0b9c47a2373f5d9ee2aa058422c19e5a1ecdee7f874bdb8b2f945178a7e3eb82", "target_id": "ru-en85-u053-b0057", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "d745ec029302e5fec77aed6d03c9a11e0e7a626768aebc546be3904b3db0ca96"}, {"source_id": "en85-u053-b0058", "target": "— Если б вы оказали мне такую любезность, мас’р Дэви, — ответил он. — Знаю, что вид ваш их малость подбодрит.", "source_sha256": "e0306922d00db4bda1bf553ab3823d2a79e658fdcf770989bd2d88365f3e3df6", "target_id": "ru-en85-u053-b0058", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "ed884debcdc8ce8623916fc80e6f60d6dabacf1a4ffd6d1eb5ac9d7bece5b7c1"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 51, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u053-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My little Dora being in good spirits, and very desirous that I should go—as I found on talking it over with her—I readily pledged myself to accompany him in accordance with his wish. Next morning, consequently, we were on the Yarmouth coach, and again travelling over the old ground.", "sha256": "205b367b68eab841021b17629a8974a0cd880fa1614e71a8c0c6b1925f5b3b8e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[60]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0060", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As we passed along the familiar street at night—Mr. Peggotty, in despite of all my remonstrances, carrying my bag—I glanced into Omer and Joram’s shop, and saw my old friend Mr. Omer there, smoking his pipe. I felt reluctant to be present, when Mr. Peggotty first met his sister and Ham; and made Mr. Omer my excuse for lingering behind.", "sha256": "af1083182c4c689cfdcb1f2e9e2e19d5358e189690295e79a0262f0910484180", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[61]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0061", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘How is Mr. Omer, after this long time?’ said I, going in.", "sha256": "468f01de838a979a21797dbfd6b1909620bcb3bb3638df536ec2a9cb9bdee145", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[62]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0062", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He fanned away the smoke of his pipe, that he might get a better view of me, and soon recognized me with great delight.", "sha256": "184b8595e066ca0227b055d7523f815e4b234e3d4c617af1e795e2752f2dc961", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[63]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0063", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I should get up, sir, to acknowledge such an honour as this visit,’ said he, ‘only my limbs are rather out of sorts, and I am wheeled about. With the exception of my limbs and my breath, howsoever, I am as hearty as a man can be, I’m thankful to say.’", "sha256": "08fa72e1ee2dd82306192276650f15cc7a516356df5140a56279224f160520e4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[64]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0064", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I congratulated him on his contented looks and his good spirits, and saw, now, that his easy-chair went on wheels.", "sha256": "5086fbdf64b61f7a48ab2c1f4c0c6d491f7929bb79d248a7d35a6aa2a4bdc35d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[65]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0065", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It’s an ingenious thing, ain’t it?’ he inquired, following the direction of my glance, and polishing the elbow with his arm. ‘It runs as light as a feather, and tracks as true as a mail-coach. Bless you, my little Minnie—my grand-daughter you know, Minnie’s child—puts her little strength against the back, gives it a shove, and away we go, as clever and merry as ever you see anything! And I tell you what—it’s a most uncommon chair to smoke a pipe in.’", "sha256": "63efb835998192b823b2ed611b6c3ac8cea6e38132ab3ebcfa3bf62570ec6f55", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[66]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0066", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I never saw such a good old fellow to make the best of a thing, and find out the enjoyment of it, as Mr. Omer. He was as radiant, as if his chair, his asthma, and the failure of his limbs, were the various branches of a great invention for enhancing the luxury of a pipe.", "sha256": "5a1a0f30d89470c9f947696191a0be8a985a638ec4102431ae4578dba8668046", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[67]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0067", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I see more of the world, I can assure you,’ said Mr. Omer, ‘in this chair, than ever I see out of it. You’d be surprised at the number of people that looks in of a day to have a chat. You really would! There’s twice as much in the newspaper, since I’ve taken to this chair, as there used to be. As to general reading, dear me, what a lot of it I do get through! That’s what I feel so strong, you know! If it had been my eyes, what should I have done? If it had been my ears, what should I have done? Being my limbs, what does it signify? Why, my limbs only made my breath shorter when I used ‘em. And now, if I want to go out into the street or down to the sands, I’ve only got to call Dick, Joram’s youngest ‘prentice, and away I go in my own carriage, like the Lord Mayor of London.’", "sha256": "56c323b3b11f6c8a30fee9dbf386a62ed2ce3c8ba8f55e13ca5b81271670ff0d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[68]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0068", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He half suffocated himself with laughing here.", "sha256": "6ae3c178021772e563791c5244d870f06e51ad9c60ee3e88b355d365f356f832", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[69]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0069", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Lord bless you!’ said Mr. Omer, resuming his pipe, ‘a man must take the fat with the lean; that’s what he must make up his mind to, in this life. Joram does a fine business. Ex-cellent business!’", "sha256": "04b497660788ea7ad1314984e10bb21b9d0ba62df63e59e77a533905f9ffdf33", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[70]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0070", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am very glad to hear it,’ said I.", "sha256": "9ba5f1427fcdb5c54e85e5d90ee027e6b676ee69c4fbe054c66591c7f112bb24", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[71]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0071", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I knew you would be,’ said Mr. Omer. ‘And Joram and Minnie are like Valentines. What more can a man expect? What’s his limbs to that!’", "sha256": "725a76af21f8f75751e911af6904417b38b79ccffe283beb4caf4c9fdebd0336", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[72]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0072", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "His supreme contempt for his own limbs, as he sat smoking, was one of the pleasantest oddities I have ever encountered.", "sha256": "26b59a211a306ea2dd84bc0296227adb75f47386a27fc4546d6bbfa4d6b8835b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[73]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0073", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And since I’ve took to general reading, you’ve took to general writing, eh, sir?’ said Mr. Omer, surveying me admiringly. ‘What a lovely work that was of yours! What expressions in it! I read it every word—every word. And as to feeling sleepy! Not at all!’", "sha256": "9b9aeb666c5e971868b90b75418965375ddf83b656f1b27c165bf01d2048e735", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[74]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0074", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I laughingly expressed my satisfaction, but I must confess that I thought this association of ideas significant.", "sha256": "15e84b37f2a0beb566e4a36ffd6d07c1fda978232a06dec0c02d2e2e32434ea4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[75]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0075", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I give you my word and honour, sir,’ said Mr. Omer, ‘that when I lay that book upon the table, and look at it outside; compact in three separate and indiwidual wollumes—one, two, three; I am as proud as Punch to think that I once had the honour of being connected with your family. And dear me, it’s a long time ago, now, ain’t it? Over at Blunderstone. With a pretty little party laid along with the other party. And you quite a small party then, yourself. Dear, dear!’", "sha256": "e3bea9254ed2f3e04bb20361474ce698874ec09959ae22db36922435e25f3161", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[76]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0076", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I changed the subject by referring to Emily. After assuring him that I did not forget how interested he had always been in her, and how kindly he had always treated her, I gave him a general account of her restoration to her uncle by the aid of Martha; which I knew would please the old man. He listened with the utmost attention, and said, feelingly, when I had done:", "sha256": "e85c04c9d532dc77c9526abe162d23c238a4c5c3951197f4e6fb90c081e98359", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[77]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0077", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am rejoiced at it, sir! It’s the best news I have heard for many a day. Dear, dear, dear! And what’s going to be undertook for that unfortunate young woman, Martha, now?’", "sha256": "f90733eeb01c372568e10974fae8adbf60731fd2905bb7b2849b7b0176a883bf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[78]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0078", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You touch a point that my thoughts have been dwelling on since yesterday,’ said I, ‘but on which I can give you no information yet, Mr. Omer. Mr. Peggotty has not alluded to it, and I have a delicacy in doing so. I am sure he has not forgotten it. He forgets nothing that is disinterested and good.’", "sha256": "55aed7c04b7e69db6643788cd09c9eea7e41134f530bd08c6fb1f9acdea283ca", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[79]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0079", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Because you know,’ said Mr. Omer, taking himself up, where he had left off, ‘whatever is done, I should wish to be a member of. Put me down for anything you may consider right, and let me know. I never could think the girl all bad, and I am glad to find she’s not. So will my daughter Minnie be. Young women are contradictory creatures in some things—her mother was just the same as her—but their hearts are soft and kind. It’s all show with Minnie, about Martha. Why she should consider it necessary to make any show, I don’t undertake to tell you. But it’s all show, bless you. She’d do her any kindness in private. So, put me down for whatever you may consider right, will you be so good? and drop me a line where to forward it. Dear me!’ said Mr. Omer, ‘when a man is drawing on to a time of life, where the two ends of life meet; when he finds himself, however hearty he is, being wheeled about for the second time, in a speeches of go-cart; he should be over-rejoiced to do a kindness if he can. He wants plenty. And I don’t speak of myself, particular,’ said Mr. Omer, ‘because, sir, the way I look at it is, that we are all drawing on to the bottom of the hill, whatever age we are, on account of time never standing still for a single moment. So let us always do a kindness, and be over-rejoiced. To be sure!’", "sha256": "8fc438bc6a110867d6caecb7720258e8cc254a808611bddb5623006160b4456a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[80]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0080", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He knocked the ashes out of his pipe, and put it on a ledge in the back of his chair, expressly made for its reception.", "sha256": "1a2e517bc11fdbbf87995564ab158bdc401cbb8ef088ffad9395e68e2164db06", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[81]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0081", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘There’s Em’ly’s cousin, him that she was to have been married to,’ said Mr. Omer, rubbing his hands feebly, ‘as fine a fellow as there is in Yarmouth! He’ll come and talk or read to me, in the evening, for an hour together sometimes. That’s a kindness, I should call it! All his life’s a kindness.’", "sha256": "ac88fb34689553438099d710edb58b92f322bbc317ca833775bc5d909bf07601", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[82]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0082", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am going to see him now,’ said I.", "sha256": "899787a0f32617d8d2d6712b96cf722f3f0d4d578650157c06c73ae0fac5d497", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[83]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0083", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Are you?’ said Mr. Omer. ‘Tell him I was hearty, and sent my respects. Minnie and Joram’s at a ball. They would be as proud to see you as I am, if they was at home. Minnie won’t hardly go out at all, you see, “on account of father”, as she says. So I swore tonight, that if she didn’t go, I’d go to bed at six. In consequence of which,’ Mr. Omer shook himself and his chair with laughter at the success of his device, ‘she and Joram’s at a ball.’", "sha256": "fc754f9861ea55430422baf60eca0900adc5898c17bdaf73e59a1a663bce21cf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[84]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0084", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I shook hands with him, and wished him good night.", "sha256": "9035ccc139138abf458f58a4e04849b4fce0b017cc1fd4a66131c4bebb8426d8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[85]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0085", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Half a minute, sir,’ said Mr. Omer. ‘If you was to go without seeing my little elephant, you’d lose the best of sights. You never see such a sight! Minnie!’ A musical little voice answered, from somewhere upstairs, ‘I am coming, grandfather!’ and a pretty little girl with long, flaxen, curling hair, soon came running into the shop.", "sha256": "a6c9ec759cc353ae0409fbb97d592bc857b381f7f819b2c0c270552a7a05055c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[86]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0086", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘This is my little elephant, sir,’ said Mr. Omer, fondling the child. ‘Siamese breed, sir. Now, little elephant!’", "sha256": "fcecd864f5ed173671ff4bdea4c7cf0f2b31969ce79212800afc68f630f11abd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[87]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0087", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The little elephant set the door of the parlour open, enabling me to see that, in these latter days, it was converted into a bedroom for Mr. Omer who could not be easily conveyed upstairs; and then hid her pretty forehead, and tumbled her long hair, against the back of Mr. Omer’s chair.", "sha256": "83412d767b01304d996766a9e2f529534fd661a5fdb68a68fbb08f49a3fd66df", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[88]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0088", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘The elephant butts, you know, sir,’ said Mr. Omer, winking, ‘when he goes at a object. Once, elephant. Twice. Three times!’", "sha256": "ddf02bf4058a2292dd6b549d30670e757d44b82fdd291243b157012cac1b732a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[89]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0089", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At this signal, the little elephant, with a dexterity that was next to marvellous in so small an animal, whisked the chair round with Mr. Omer in it, and rattled it off, pell-mell, into the parlour, without touching the door-post: Mr. Omer indescribably enjoying the performance, and looking back at me on the road as if it were the triumphant issue of his life’s exertions.", "sha256": "b733abe2005d1d2ec969fe89c66ce0f4d6aabf6008de5a9ce32d3d1e1264e6dd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[90]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0090", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "After a stroll about the town I went to Ham’s house. Peggotty had now removed here for good; and had let her own house to the successor of Mr. Barkis in the carrying business, who had paid her very well for the good-will, cart, and horse. I believe the very same slow horse that Mr. Barkis drove was still at work.", "sha256": "fe34399cd407f03708d04f72282e1538e55c36deac862c9d5985848735e683a0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[91]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
